_meta.purpose: Literature prior-best / ceiling reference for BioDecisionBench (benchmark_v2) prior-best comparison table
_meta.verified_semantics: verified=true means the number was transcribed directly from the named table/figure/section of the cited source during this collection run. self-prior entries are our own numbers: verified=true = read from a local document that states the result (working manuscript / internal leaderboard), NOT peer-reviewed literature.
corrections: Task brief cited DNABERT-2 as arXiv:2306.15794; in arXiv that ID is HyenaDNA (Nguyen et al.). DNABERT-2 (GUE benchmark) is arXiv:2306.15006 (ICLR 2024). Both were used; HyenaDNA:2306.15794 is the source of the 8-subset GenomicBenchmarks accuracy table.
Task brief cited TAPE as arXiv:1903.00089; that ID resolves to a different paper here. TAPE is arXiv:1906.08230 'Evaluating Protein Transfer Learning with TAPE' (verified title match).
Genomic Benchmarks brief cited bioRxiv 10.1101/2022.06.08.495248; the open-access journal version is BMC Genomic Data 24:25 (2023), PMC10150520, which is the table-bearing source used here.
GUE metric in the DNABERT-2 paper is MCC (F1 only for Covid Variant Classification), not accuracy/F1 as assumed in the brief - see per-family notes.
DeepSTARR original paper reports Pearson correlation (PCC), not Spearman - see family notes.
not_obtained: ProteinGym current-leaderboard values for IPTM (and any post-v1.2 model): ProteinGym leaderboard export zero_shot_substitutions_scores.zip is 1.91 GB and only ~230 MB was retrievable in 5 min from marks.hms.harvard.edu; PosiTrain/IPTM paper not found via arXiv search, Europe PMC or OpenAlex in this environment.
DeepSTARR official Spearman on dev_test/hk_test splits (author-reported Spearman does not exist; only PCC). Secondary replication Spearman values are included, flagged.
RNAcompete per-RBP sequence->z-score regression prior-best (Spearman/MAE): no published leaderboard exists; only the original paper's motif-quality numbers (AUROC vs in vivo data) are citable.

Per-dataset (not per-category) accuracies for lg_* / dna_* / protein_homology_* tasks from our own earlier work: LLaMA-Gene Table 9 is category-level only; BioPAWS-1/BioPAWS-2/EMERGENCE per-task tables (bioRxiv 2026.01.03.697478) and the biopaws/ result .jsonl files are not present in this environment.
AUROC numbers for the Genomic Benchmarks CNN baseline: the GB paper reports accuracy and F1 only (string 'AUROC' absent from the paper text).
Genomic Benchmarks mouse_enhancers AUROC in Nat Commun benchmarking paper: dataset-name mapping to 'Enhancer' row not stated explicitly; recorded as unverified.

RNAcompete.source: RNAcompete (Ray et al., Nature 498:173 (2013), author manuscript PMC3929597)
RNAcompete.note: Scope reference for our 14-RBP Score subset: '~240,000 short (30-41 nt) RNAs containing all 9-mers >=16x', pool split into two halves for internal cross-validation; per-7-mer Z (intensity) and E (rank) scores. Our family uses probe_metadata.tsv x probe_zscore.tsv per RBP, so 'score' is in units of array z-scores, not Kd.

RNAcompete.source: RNAcompete (Ray et al., Nature 498:173 (2013), author manuscript PMC3929597)
RNAcompete.note: Verbatim: 'for QKI (quaking), the AUROC for the RNAcompete motif was 93% versus 83% for the literature motif' (Fig 1c, Supplementary Data 5). This is the closest published 'quality ceiling' for the family: motif-level classification AUROC up to ~0.93 against in vivo data.

RNAcompete.source: RNAcompete (Ray et al., Nature 498:173 (2013), author manuscript PMC3929597)
RNAcompete.note: Reported failure case: 'the RNAcompete motif for FUS produced an AUROC <0.5 when compared to in vivo crosslinking-based data for both FUS and its paralogue TAF15'. Only one such case in the paper - a useful calibration caveat (in vitro specificity need not transfer in vivo).

RNAcompete.source: RNAcompete (Ray et al., Nature 498:173 (2013), author manuscript PMC3929597)
RNAcompete.note: 'In almost all cases, E scores for 7-mers from the two halves of the RNAcompete pool for a given protein are more similar to each other than to those of other assayed proteins' (Fig 1b). Missing: no numeric replicate correlation (r/ρ) is printed in the main text, so we cannot quote an intrinsic Spearman ceiling for per-probe z-score prediction - a gap for our Score-family ceiling discussion.
